statement.essentials: During the operation the surgeon can touch a tissue with a small stimulator: if it is the nerve, the face twitches. The patient is kept from being paralysed so this can be seen.
statement.anatomy: A hand-held stimulator or a monitor helps localise the nerve by the facial movement it causes; muscle relaxants are reversed beforehand, and local anaesthetic is kept away from the nerve because it may block it.

limitations: One institution’s protocol; the same protocol notes that monitoring has become routine and is most useful for recurrent tumours or difficult dissections.
